doc:001.title: Informed Consent Form for Frozen Section Pathological Examination
doc:001.content:
Diagnosis: Breast mass
Information provided
Intraoperative rapid frozen-section pathological examination involves rapidly freezing lesion tissue excised and submitted for examination during surgery, preparing it into sections, and conducting histological observation under a microscope. Its purpose is to preliminarily determine the nature of the lesion or determine the status of the surgical margins and other circumstances, thereby providing reference opinions for clinicians in determining the intraoperative treatment plan. However, because of the limitations of sampling for frozen-section preparation, the short time available, and the considerable variability in tissues and cells caused by low-temperature freezing during frozen sectioning, the accuracy of frozen-section diagnosis is limited. Therefore, the relevant matters are hereby explained as follows:
1. The frozen-section diagnosis of a single specimen must be completed within 30 minutes; the same applies successively to additional specimens.
2. For some cases in which a definitive diagnosis is difficult to make, delayed diagnosis or waiting for the paraffin-section report is permitted.
3. Because of sampling limitations, frozen-section results may sometimes be inconsistent with the final routine paraffin-section report.
4. Rapid frozen-section pathological examination serves only as a reference for clinical surgical treatment and cannot be used as the final pathological diagnosis. The final pathological diagnosis must be made based on paraffin sections.
Patients and their family members are requested to carefully read and understand the above circumstances before signing and have the right to choose whether to undergo intraoperative frozen-section examination. If the patient and/or family members refuse to sign after reading and understanding the information, the pathologist may refuse to perform an intraoperative rapid frozen-section pathological examination for the patient.
Precautions
The physician in charge has explained to me in detail the importance of intraoperative rapid frozen-section pathological examination and its precautions, and I have carefully read the above provisions and accurately understood their meaning. I agree to undergo intraoperative rapid frozen-section pathological examination. If the results of the intraoperative rapid frozen-section pathological examination are inconsistent with the final routine pathological results, resulting in changes to the treatment plan and treatment outcomes, I undertake not to hold the pathologist or hospital liable on this basis. This is certified by my signature.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

doc:003.title: Initial Progress Note of Breast Surgery
doc:003.content:
Right breast mass detected on physical examination half a month ago
Half a month ago, a physical examination detected a mass in the patient's right breast, measuring approximately 1 cm. It had poor mobility and no tenderness. There was no localized ulceration, redness, or swelling of the breast skin, no thinning of the skin, no visible dilated subcutaneous veins, and no eczematous changes of the nipple skin. There was no nipple discharge. 2124-07-17, mammography at this hospital: scattered fibroglandular tissue in both breasts; mass in the upper inner quadrant of the right breast, provisionally classified as BI-RADS category 4C. For further diagnosis and treatment, the patient was admitted from the outpatient clinic with a provisional diagnosis of “right breast mass, suspected carcinoma.” Since onset, the patient has been alert, with fair mental status, sleep, and appetite; bowel movements and urination have been normal, and there has been no significant increase or decrease in body weight.

doc:004.title: First ward-round note by the attending physician of breast surgery
doc:004.content: The patient had no history of consuming hormone-containing foods or medications and no family history of breast cancer. 1, breast mass (right breast, suspected cancer) 2, diabetes mellitus 1, the patient is an elderly woman 2, admitted because a right breast mass had been found on physical examination half a month earlier. 3, physical examination showed symmetrical breasts; the skin of both breasts showed no redness, swelling, ulceration, retraction, or peau d'orange changes; the bilateral nipples were at the same level, without retraction or deviation, and without eczematous changes. No old surgical scars were seen. A mass measuring approximately 1.5 cm in diameter was palpable in the upper inner right breast; it was hard, had limited mobility and poorly defined borders, and showed no adhesion to the skin or obvious tenderness. There was no discharge. No definite mass was palpable in the contralateral breast. No abnormally enlarged lymph nodes were palpable in either axilla or either supraclavicular region. 4, ancillary examination: 2124-07-17 mammography at this hospital: scattered fibroglandular tissue in both breasts; a mass in the upper inner quadrant of the right breast, considered BI-RADS category 4C; a few patchy calcifications in both breasts, considered BI-RADS category 2. Calcification of the vascular walls in both breasts. Please correlate with the clinical examination; further ultrasonography and MR examination, as well as follow-up, are recommended. 1. Lobular hyperplasia of the breast: lobular hyperplasia of the breast is common in premenopausal women, with breast pain related to the menstrual cycle and a nodular sensation of breast thickening on physical examination as its main clinical manifestations. The breast pain has no fixed location, may persist throughout the entire menstrual cycle, and is relieved after the onset of menstruation; on examination, a nodular sensation or localized thickening may be palpable in the upper outer quadrant of the breast. This patient is an elderly woman; the mass has poorly defined borders and no skin adhesion, and no enlarged lymph nodes were palpable in the ipsilateral axilla; therefore, the findings are inconsistent with this diagnosis. 2. Fat necrosis of the breast: this is more common in middle-aged and elderly women with a history of breast trauma, and the breast mass remains unchanged or decreases in size over a long period. The mass is hard, has poorly defined borders and poor mobility, and may be accompanied by skin redness and swelling or adhesion to the skin. Fine-needle aspiration or excisional biopsy is helpful for differentiation. This patient is a 69-year-old woman; the mass has poorly defined borders and no skin adhesion, and no enlarged lymph nodes were palpable in the ipsilateral axilla; therefore, the findings are inconsistent with this diagnosis. 1. The patient has completed a complete blood count, liver and kidney function tests, electrolyte and blood glucose tests, routine urinalysis, and coagulation function tests. No contraindications to surgery were identified. The specific treatment plan will be determined after the patient completes the preoperative imaging examinations.

doc:005.title: Initial Ward Round Record by the Chief Physician, Breast Surgery
doc:005.content: A right breast mass was found on physical examination half a month ago. Based on the patient's medical history, physical examination, and ancillary examinations, breast cancer is currently the leading clinical consideration. The specific pathological type still requires histopathological confirmation to guide the formulation of the further treatment plan; therefore, core needle biopsy of the right breast mass may be performed. Given the possibility of a false-negative result with breast core needle biopsy, if the core needle biopsy is inconclusive, surgical biopsy may be performed in conjunction with the clinical stage of the tumor, with excision of the right breast mass and submission for intraoperative frozen-section pathological examination to guide the extent of further surgery and establish the pathology, thereby determining the surgical approach. 1. Continue to complete the examinations. 2. Based on the patient's medical history, physical examination, and ancillary examinations, malignancy is highly likely. Right breast mass core needle biopsy is planned under local anesthesia today to determine the pathological nature of the mass. The patient and family were informed preoperatively of the necessity and risks of the procedure.

doc:021.title: Preoperative Informed Consent Form for Core Needle Biopsy of a Breast Mass
doc:021.content: Preoperative examination result: Right breast mass. Preoperative proposed diagnosis: □ Left breast ■ Right breast □ Left axilla □ Right axilla mass. Proposed procedure: □ Left breast ■ Right breast □ Left axilla □ Right axilla mass core needle biopsy. Information disclosed: Based on the patient's condition, a core needle biopsy of the breast mass is required to establish a definitive diagnosis and assess treatment efficacy. The biopsy may cause the following adverse complications: I. Intraoperative: 1, the procedure is performed under local anesthesia, and there is a possibility of allergic reactions to anesthetic agents, including respiratory arrest and cardiac arrest. 2, pain during the biopsy, with stress reactions such as dizziness and cold sweats occurring during the procedure. 3, if the patient has concomitant cardiac, cerebral, pulmonary, or other diseases, the pre-existing disease may suddenly worsen intraoperatively (including postoperatively), potentially resulting in an accident or even death. 4, uncontrollable bleeding or oozing that may be life-threatening. II. Postoperative: 1, pain and bleeding at the biopsy site, hematoma formation, subcutaneous bruising and ecchymosis, and fluid accumulation. 2, persistent bleeding or oozing; another operation may also be required to achieve hemostasis. 3, failure of the core needle biopsy to obtain tissue, possibly requiring another biopsy on a later date. 4, further decline in the function of pre-existing cardiac, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, or other organs. 5, stress ulcer bleeding and hemorrhagic shock. 6, biopsy-site infection, including incision infection or systemic infection (such as bacteremia or sepsis). 7, in patients with diabetes, the incidence of each of the above complications is significantly increased. 8, postoperative systemic complications resulting in death. 9, accidents that current medical science is not yet able to explain or resolve. Alternative medical plan: If the patient or authorized representative does not understand the aforementioned surgical risks and complications, they may consult the physician and, after fully understanding them, decide whether to choose surgical treatment or proceed according to an alternative medical plan. Please write your opinion in the text and sign it. Precautions: 1, if the patient (or authorized representative) truly still does not understand the above discussion or finds the potentially serious consequences difficult to accept, please do not sign and postpone the procedure. 2, the patient (or authorized representative) should understand clearly: signing this record indicates that the patient (or authorized representative) has fully understood the possibility of the aforementioned accidents and complications and is fully mentally prepared for them. Please complete this form after careful consideration. 3, this consent form has legal effect and may be submitted to a court as evidence.

However, because patients differ in their psychological status and capacity to cope, and because disease progression is unpredictable, to facilitate treatment, please now authorize and appoint an agent whom you fully trust to exercise the patient's right to informed consent on the patient's behalf. In accordance with current applicable laws and regulations in the local jurisdiction, when the patient has a certain degree of understanding and judgment, the right to make decisions about surgery and the right to sign belong to the patient. However, when the patient has limited or no capacity for civil conduct, a person may be appointed to exercise the right to sign on the patient's behalf according to the following order: spouse—parents—adult children—other relatives—other relatives or friends designated by a grassroots organization or court. When the patient has full capacity for civil conduct, the patient may also appoint a relative or organization to exercise the right to informed consent; however, an “Authorization and Power of Attorney” jointly signed by the patient and the appointed agent must be retained as proof. Findings: Several enlarged lymph nodes of varying sizes were seen in the left supraclavicular region, one of which measured approximately 15.2 × 7.9mm. No fusion between the lymph nodes was seen. Findings: At approximately the 12-1 o'clock position in the right breast, a 14.5 × 7.9 × 8.1mm mass is visualized, located 7mm from the body surface. It demonstrates a horizontal growth orientation and an irregular shape. The margins of the mass are indistinct, with a hyperechoic halo. The interior is hypoechoic, with scattered fine punctate hyperechoic foci. There is no significant change in the echoes posterior to the mass, no distortion of the structures surrounding the mass, and no significant changes in the ducts surrounding the mass. CFI shows mildly abundant blood-flow signals at the periphery within the mass; the vessels are relatively large and tortuous. After intravenous injection of 2.4ml of the contrast agent SonoVue through a limb vein, the mass demonstrates a centripetal perfusion pattern. At peak perfusion, the mass shows low-intensity perfusion, with indistinct boundaries and heterogeneous perfusion. Perforating vessels are visible around it, and the perfusion extent is similar to that on grayscale imaging.
Conclusion: Solid mass at the 12-1 o'clock position of the right breast: proposed US BI-RADS category 4C; please correlate clinically.
Clinical diagnosis: Breast mass
